title: Hydraulic lifter tick
one_line: Lifter loses pressure then ticks until oil pressure stabilizes.
quick_test: Cold start: if tick fades within 30–90s, lifter/tensioner climbs.

title: Timing chain tensioner rattle
one_line: Chain slack rattles briefly before full oil pressure tightens it.
quick_test: Cold start: 1–3s rattle then gone strongly fits tensioner.

title: Light timing tensioner noise
one_line: Mild start-up chatter from early chain slack.
quick_test: If it’s only cold and disappears fast, it’s usually tensioner/guide behavior.

title: Timing chain guides worn
one_line: Worn guides let the chain slap/rattle especially on decel/load transitions.
quick_test: Rattle strongest on lift-off (decel) points to guide/tension behavior.

title: VVT cam phaser rattle
one_line: Phaser control can rattle when oil control is unstable under certain conditions.
quick_test: Warm + under load rattle that stops when lifting can fit phaser/ping separation.

title: VVT control issue
one_line: Timing control drift can cause abnormal combustion or valvetrain noise under load.
quick_test: If symptom appears with acceleration and improves with steady throttle, VVT/ping rises.

title: Normal injector tick
one_line: Many engines (especially direct injection) tick rhythmically and it’s normal.
quick_test: If it’s light, steady, no performance issues, and tracks RPM evenly—often normal.

title: Valve train tap
one_line: Top-end tap can be lash/rocker/lifter behavior that tracks RPM.
quick_test: If it’s loudest from top engine and speeds up with RPM in park, valve train rises.

title: Light valve train tick
one_line: Light top-end tick from valvetrain components.
quick_test: Rev to 1500: if it stays light/clean and no symptoms, it’s usually not urgent.

title: Severe valvetrain issue
one_line: Harsh grinding/tapping may indicate severe top-end mechanical contact.
quick_test: If noise is loud at idle in park and worsens quickly, treat as urgent.

title: Exhaust leak tick/tap
one_line: Small manifold leak ticks like a sewing machine, faster with RPM.
quick_test: Cold start near manifold: sharp tick that changes as it warms suggests leak.

title: Warm manifold leak
one_line: Expansion can open a leak and create warm-only ticking.
quick_test: If tick appears warm-only and sharp near manifold area, leak rises.

title: Exhaust leak louder under load
one_line: Under load, exhaust pressure increases and the leak ticks louder.
quick_test: If tick is strongest during acceleration and quiet on coast, exhaust leak rises.

title: Exhaust heat shield rattle
one_line: Loose shield buzzes/rattles at certain RPM or on decel.
quick_test: Tap shield (cool) to reproduce the same buzz.

title: Loose exhaust hanger
one_line: Hanger slack lets exhaust move and rattle on bumps/load change.
quick_test: Rattle more on lift-off or bumps often matches hanger slack.

title: Internal exhaust baffle rattle
one_line: Inside resonator/muffler baffles can break and rattle at certain RPM.
quick_test: Hold RPM at the rattle range while parked—if it happens, it’s exhaust/body, not wheels.

title: Heat shield rattle
one_line: Thin shields buzz at a narrow frequency band.
quick_test: Touch/press suspected shield (cool) and see if rattle changes.

title: Loose engine cover
one_line: Plastic cover resonates and rattles at certain RPM.
quick_test: Press lightly on cover at idle—if rattle changes, you found it.

title: Loose undertray/liner
one_line: Undertray or wheel-well liner flaps and rattles with speed/wind.
quick_test: If it appears only above a certain speed and not in park revving, undertray rises.

title: Loose wheel well liner
one_line: Missing clips cause liner to flap and rattle with speed.
quick_test: Visual check for missing fasteners; noise often changes with wind/speed not RPM.

title: Loose brake dust shield
one_line: Shield touches rotor and makes scrape/squeal/rattle with speed.
quick_test: Light brake: if noise changes instantly, shield/stone/brakes rise.

title: Dust shield contact
one_line: Bent dust shield scrapes the rotor and follows wheel speed.
quick_test: Noise follows speed and may change when braking lightly.

title: Stone in brake area
one_line: Small stone trapped can squeal/scrape with wheel rotation.
quick_test: Reverse slowly: sometimes the tone changes with a trapped stone.

title: Stone in tire tread
one_line: Rhythmic tap follows speed like a metronome—often just a stone.
quick_test: Inspect tread quickly; remove stone and the tap disappears.

title: Brake pads to metal
one_line: Pad material is gone—metal backing plate grinds the rotor.
quick_test: Grinding gets worse when braking = pads-to-metal highly likely.

title: Brake wear indicator squeal
one_line: A small metal tab squeals when pads are near end of life.
quick_test: Light braking at 20–30 mph: squeal changes immediately.

title: Glazed pads/rotors
one_line: Overheated surfaces get glossy and squeal with weaker bite.
quick_test: Squeal + less initial bite after hard braking suggests glazing.

title: Brake dust/debris noise
one_line: Debris between pad/rotor causes intermittent squeal.
quick_test: If it comes/goes and changes with braking, debris is plausible.

title: Stuck caliper
one_line: Caliper doesn’t release fully, overheats one wheel and can grind.
quick_test: After short drive, one wheel much hotter than others = stuck caliper clue.

title: Loose brake hardware/clips
one_line: Pad clips/hardware rattle—often stops with light brake pressure.
quick_test: Light brake touch: if rattle stops instantly, hardware rises.

title: Loose caliper bolt
one_line: Dangerous—caliper movement can clunk and reduce braking safety.
quick_test: If brake rattle is heavy and changes with braking, inspect bolts urgently.

title: Wheel bearing hum/whine
one_line: Noise follows speed and changes when the car weight shifts left/right.
quick_test: Gentle lane change: if noise changes, bearing rises.

title: Wheel bearing noise (general)
one_line: Speed-related hum/whine that reacts to load shift.
quick_test: Lane change test separates bearing from tire noise.

title: Severe wheel bearing failure
one_line: Bearing can grind/knock with vibration—safety risk.
quick_test: If noise is loud + vibration + heat at hub, treat as urgent.

title: Loose lug nuts
one_line: Wheel can wobble/knock—this is an immediate safety stop.
quick_test: If clunk + wobble: stop and verify lug tightness immediately.

title: CV axle outer joint
one_line: Rhythmic clicking on turns is classic outer CV joint.
quick_test: Full-lock slow turn in a parking lot: clicking = CV joint.

title: Tie rod end play
one_line: Steering looseness and clunks from worn tie rod ends.
quick_test: Steering left/right at standstill: clunk + looseness suggests tie rod play.

title: Strut mount clunk
one_line: Top strut mount can clunk when turning or over bumps.
quick_test: Low-speed turn + bumps: clunk from one corner fits strut mount.

title: Worn sway bar link
one_line: Common clunk/rattle over small bumps at low speed.
quick_test: If it repeats on small bumps and doesn’t care about braking, link rises.

title: Control arm bushing wear
one_line: Bushing slack clunks under braking and load transfer.
quick_test: Clunk changes with light braking over bumps = bushing clue.

title: Ball joint play
one_line: Ball joint play can clunk and is safety-critical if severe.
quick_test: Clunk + wandering steering + uneven tire wear raises suspicion.

title: Serpentine belt slip
one_line: Cold squeal that fades is usually belt slip on start-up load.
quick_test: Cold start squeal 1–10s then gone = belt slip pattern.

title: Light belt slip
one_line: Minor slip can sound like a whine/squeal under load.
quick_test: Add load (lights/defrost): if noise increases, belt slip rises.

title: Weak belt tensioner
one_line: Tensioner can’t hold belt tension, causes squeal/rattle and belt wear.
quick_test: Noise worse on start and with load suggests weak tensioner.

title: Belt misalignment
one_line: Misaligned pulley makes belt squeal persistently.
quick_test: Squeal constant warm + belt tracking off-center suggests misalignment.

title: Idler pulley bearing
one_line: Worn idler bearing whines and can seize later.
quick_test: Whine localized at one pulley area; changes with RPM.

title: Pulley bearing (general)
one_line: Bearing noise can be whine, squeal, or grind depending on severity.
quick_test: If A/C toggle doesn’t change it and noise is front accessory, pulley bearing rises.

title: Idler bearing failure
one_line: Grinding indicates bearing is near failure and can throw the belt.
quick_test: Grinding localized at one pulley = urgent bearing.

title: Alternator bearing
one_line: Alternator bearing can whine with RPM and worsen under electrical load.
quick_test: Turn on high electrical load: if whine changes, alternator rises.

title: Alternator bearing failure
one_line: Grinding alternator bearing can fail suddenly and you’ll lose charging.
quick_test: Grinding from alternator area + charging symptoms = urgent.

title: Alternator whine (bearing/diode)
one_line: Whine tracking RPM can be bearing noise or electrical diode whine.
quick_test: Load test (lights/defrost): change in whine supports alternator involvement.

title: Power steering pump whine
one_line: Pump whines more when steering is turned or fluid/air issues exist.
quick_test: Turn wheel slightly at idle: if whine changes, PS pump rises.

title: Low PS fluid/air in system
one_line: Low fluid or air makes the pump whine, especially cold.
quick_test: Whine changes with steering input; check reservoir level (if hydraulic PS).

title: A/C compressor bearing
one_line: A/C clutch/bearing can grind/whine especially when engaged.
quick_test: Toggle A/C on/off: if noise changes, compressor path rises.

title: A/C clutch rattle
one_line: Clutch can rattle at idle or during engagement cycles.
quick_test: Noise appears/disappears with A/C toggling or cycling.

title: A/C clutch bearing squeal
one_line: Squeal can come from clutch bearing and worsen warm.
quick_test: A/C on/off changes squeal = clutch bearing clue.

title: Normal A/C refrigerant hiss
one_line: Brief hiss when A/C cycles can be normal expansion noise.
quick_test: If it correlates exactly with A/C cycling, it’s often normal.

title: Water pump bearing
one_line: Bearing can whine and later leak/overheat.
quick_test: Warm-only front noise + overheating complaint raises water pump.

title: Water pump bearing (hot)
one_line: Some bearings get louder after warming.
quick_test: If noise starts after warm-up and grows, treat as urgent bearing.

title: Cooling fan/shroud contact
one_line: Fan can rub shroud and make whine/rattle when it kicks on.
quick_test: If noise appears exactly when fan turns on, fan contact rises.

title: Vacuum leak
one_line: Unmetered air causes hiss and often rough/lean idle.
quick_test: Idle changes with throttle blip; lean codes (P0171) support it.

title: Vacuum hose leak
one_line: Small hose crack hisses at idle and can cause lean symptoms.
quick_test: If hiss is strongest at idle and reduces with throttle, hose leak rises.

title: Intake gasket leak
one_line: Gasket leak hisses and causes lean/rough idle especially cold.
quick_test: Lean idle + hiss that changes with temperature supports gasket leak.

title: PCV valve issue
one_line: PCV stuck/open can hiss and disturb idle/fuel trim.
quick_test: If idle hunts and hiss is near PCV area, PCV rises.

title: PCV valve stuck
one_line: Stuck PCV can create steady hiss and rough idle.
quick_test: Cold idle rough then stabilizes supports PCV/vacuum path.

title: Brake booster vacuum leak
one_line: Booster leak hisses and can change brake feel.
quick_test: If idle changes when pressing brake pedal, booster leak rises.

title: Turbo boost leak
one_line: Hiss under acceleration with power loss fits boost leak.
quick_test: If hiss appears only on boost/accel and power dropped, boost leak rises.

title: Intercooler/boost hose leak
one_line: Hose split can hiss under load and reduce power.
quick_test: Under-load hiss + sudden power loss points to hose leak.

title: Intake air leak
one_line: Air leak can hiss when airflow increases and can affect mixture.
quick_test: If hiss scales with throttle and engine feels weak, intake leak rises.

title: Post-MAF leak
one_line: Leak after MAF causes lean running and can hiss under load.
quick_test: Lean codes + hiss under throttle supports post-MAF leak.

title: Detonation / ping
one_line: Combustion knock under acceleration, usually higher pitch than rod knock.
quick_test: If it appears only on accel and improves with higher octane once, ping rises.

title: Spark knock / ping
one_line: Timing/fuel/heat can cause ping under load.
quick_test: Only under load + disappears on lift = ping behavior.

title: Pre-ignition / severe knock risk
one_line: Severe combustion knock can damage pistons quickly.
quick_test: If knock is harsh under load and power drops, stop pushing throttle immediately.

title: Spark plug issue
one_line: Wrong gap/heat range or worn plug can promote ping/misfire.
quick_test: If under-load ping + misfire symptoms, plugs/ignition rises.

title: EGR/lean condition
one_line: Lean mixture or EGR issues can increase knock under load.
quick_test: If ping appears after warm-up and fuel trims/lean codes present, lean path rises.

title: Rod bearing knock
one_line: Deep knock that worsens under load—serious bottom-end wear.
quick_test: Deep knock follows RPM and gets louder with load = rod bearing pattern.

title: Early rod bearing noise
one_line: Early knock can be subtle but load-related.
quick_test: If knock increases with acceleration and persists even in park revving, treat seriously.

title: Piston slap
one_line: Cold knock that fades warm on some engines due to skirt clearance.
quick_test: If cold-only knock fades as warm, piston slap rises.

title: Harmonic balancer / crank pulley failure
one_line: Balancer separation can knock/clunk and cause belt issues.
quick_test: If pulley looks like it wobbles (image/video), balancer rises.

title: Crank pulley wobble
one_line: Wobble causes vibration/noise and can throw the belt.
quick_test: Visual wobble at crank pulley is a strong indicator.

title: Engine mount clunk
one_line: Worn mount allows engine to shift and clunk on throttle on/off.
quick_test: Clunk happens exactly when you go on/off throttle, not with steady RPM.

title: Mount / drivetrain movement issue
one_line: Mount slack transmits clunks/rattles during load transitions.
quick_test: D↔R shift clunk and throttle tip-in clunk supports mount/driveline play.

title: Differential whine
one_line: Whine follows speed and often changes with throttle load.
quick_test: Same speed, throttle on/off: if whine changes, diff rises.

title: Warm differential whine
one_line: Diff noise can appear/shift after warming, often load-related.
quick_test: If it’s worse warm and changes with throttle, diff rises.

title: Decel differential whine
one_line: Some diffs whine more on coast than on throttle.
quick_test: If it’s loudest on lift-off at the same speed, decel diff whine rises.

title: Transmission whine
one_line: Whine tied to speed/load can come from transmission gearing/bearings.
quick_test: If whine changes with gear selection or load at same speed, trans rises.

title: Transmission whine on decel
one_line: Whine can be louder on coast depending on wear pattern.
quick_test: Same speed, lift throttle: louder on coast suggests decel trans/diff noise.

title: Differential backlash/clunk
one_line: Slack in gears causes clunk on throttle on/off.
quick_test: Clunk exactly during throttle tip-in/off, not steady speed.

title: Driveshaft U-joint play
one_line: RWD driveline play can clunk/rattle on load transitions.
quick_test: Clunk when shifting D↔R and on/off throttle suggests driveline play.

title: Tire cupping/road roar
one_line: Uneven tire wear makes roaring/whining that follows speed and road surface.
quick_test: Change pavement: tire noise often changes noticeably.

title: External wind noise
one_line: Wind noise appears at highway speed and doesn’t track RPM or throttle.
quick_test: If it’s the same at steady speed regardless of throttle, wind/liner rises.

title: Fan shroud contact
one_line: Fan/shroud rub can rattle/whine at certain times.
quick_test: Noise appears with fan activation, not with RPM alone.

title: Loose pulley/tensioner
one_line: Play in tensioner/pulley causes rattle and can throw the belt.
quick_test: Front rattle that scales with RPM and accessory load suggests pulley/tensioner play.

title: A/C clutch click
one_line: A/C clutch engagement can click/tap as it cycles—often normal unless harsh.
quick_test: If it matches A/C cycling exactly, it’s likely clutch engagement sound.

title: Loose bracket/fastener tap
one_line: A loose bracket can tap at a resonance RPM.
quick_test: If pressing on the area changes the tap, it’s external hardware.

title: EVAP purge/valve noise
one_line: Some purge valves click/hiss lightly during normal operation.
quick_test: Light repetitive ticking near purge valve with no other symptoms can be normal.

title: Needs isolation data
one_line: Diagnosis requires RPM vs speed vs load relation to avoid guessing.
quick_test: Answer one question: does the sound change with RPM while parked, or only with road speed?

title: Needs relation data
one_line: Without relation tests, multiple causes overlap.
quick_test: Tell me: cold-only or warm-only, and does it follow RPM or speed?

title: Needs isolation test
one_line: One isolation test will separate engine/accessory from wheel/drivetrain noise.
quick_test: Rev in park (engine test) vs steady-speed lane shift (wheel test).
